notes:
New Hampshire's recurring entity-level levy on an LLC is the Business Enterprise Tax (BET) of RSA 77-E. RSA 77-E:1, III defines a business enterprise to include a limited liability company and subjects each business enterprise to the tax as a separate entity; RSA 77-E:2 imposes the tax at 0.55% on the taxable enterprise value tax base for all taxable periods ending on or after December 31, 2022. The enterprise value tax base is the sum of compensation paid or accrued, interest paid or accrued, and dividends paid (RSA 77-E:1, IX), so basis is composite and the notes name the three components. The statute states no minimum tax; a return is required only where gross business receipts exceed $250,000 or the enterprise value tax base exceeds $250,000, thresholds the commissioner adjusts biennially for inflation (RSA 77-E:5, I; the figures printed in the statute are the starting amounts). For a partnership-taxed LLC the return is due on or before the fifteenth day of the third month following the end of its taxable period. There is no first-year exemption: the tax applies to every business enterprise for all taxable periods ending on or after December 31, 2022.
The Business Profits Tax (RSA 77-A) accompanies the BET: RSA 77-A:1, I defines a business organization to include an LLC, and RSA 77-A:2 imposes a 7.5% tax on the taxable business profits of every business organization. It is an entity-level tax on profits - the income measure of the two-tax regime - and is recorded as the second levy rather than in stateIncomeTax, whose fields describe the state's posture toward pass-through taxation of members.
collectedWithAnnualReport is false: root states.json carries annual_report_fee 102 for New Hampshire, the Secretary of State's annual report fee, a separate payment with no tax to overlap.
stateIncomeTax: New Hampshire has no individual income tax. RSA chapter 77, Taxation of Incomes, is repealed effective January 1, 2025, so members owe no personal income tax on pass-through income (passThroughApplies is false) and there is no pass-through entity tax election to offer: the entity itself pays the Business Profits Tax under RSA 77-A:2, which is mandatory rather than elective. topRatePercent is null because no broad-based individual income tax exists.
needsReview: The Department of Revenue Administration's own BET and BPT pages (revenue.nh.gov) are Akamai-walled to scripted clients on this route, so the record is statute-only from gencourt.state.nh.us. The RSA text carries every recorded value; what would settle the residual questions is the DRA's current-year threshold notices (the $250,000 BET and $92,000 BPT figures are the statutory starting amounts, adjusted biennially by the commissioner) and any published statement of the LLC's annual obligations in the DRA's own words.
